## Background 


There are many *graphic systems* in R for making plots and figures. These include **"base R graphics"** like the `plot()` and add-on packages like **ggplot2**. 

Let's compare how we make a simple graph with these two systems: 

We can use the in-built `cars` dataset: 

```{r}
head(cars)
```

A base R plot: 

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now for **ggplot2**.
Before I can use ggplot2 I need to install it on my computer. 
To do this we can use the function `install.packages("ggplot2")` 

>**N.B** We never run an `install.packages()` in our quarto doc (we can run it in our R console) as it would re-install the package every time I render my document. 

Once installed we still need to load it up the package into our R session. We do this with a `library()` call 

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 inputs: 

- the **data** (a data.frame of the stuff we want to plot)
- the **aesthetics** (how the data maps to the plot), 
- the **geom** layer (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point()
```

## Let's add some features (more layers)

Let's add a trend line that shows the relationship between `speed` and `distance` 

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point()
```


```{r}
ggplot(cars) + 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se=FALSE) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x="Speed MPH", 
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)" , 
       title="Stopping distance of some old cars")
```



## Gene Expression Plot 

First we will read some expression data for the effects of a GLP-1 drug

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) + 
  geom_point()  + 
  scale_colour_manual( values=c("lightblue","pink","purple") ) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x="No Drug", y="Drug", title="GLP-1 Inhibitor Effects on Gene Expression")
  

```

> Q. Use the `nrow()` function to find out how many genes are in this dataset. What is your answer?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

> Q. Use the `table()` function on the `State` column of this data.frame to find out how many ‘up’ regulated genes there are. What is your answer?

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```

> Q. Use the `colnames()` function and the `ncol()` function on the genes data frame to find out what the column names are (we will need these later) and how many columns there are. How many columns did you find?

```{r}
colnames(genes)
```


```{r}
ncol(genes)
```


```{r}
round( table(genes$State)/nrow(genes) * 100, 2 )
```


## Going Further 

Here we read the famous *gapmider* dataset: 

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url) 
head(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many entries in this dataset? 

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many different "country" values are in this dataset? 

```{r}
length( table(gapminder$country) ) 
```

```{r}
length( unique(gapminder$country) )
```

Let's make our first plot of `gdpPercap` vs `lifeExp` : 


```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp) + 
  geom_point()
```

Adding transparency to the points. 

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.25)
```

Adding color to the different continents. 

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, color=continent) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.25)
```

One useful layer we can add to explore big datasets like this is called "facetting"

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent) + 
  geom_point() +
facet_wrap(~continent)
```

### Limit to 1966 and 2004 

We can install and use the **dplyr** package to help us "filter" the full dataset down to a smaller subset that only includes the years we want. 

First we need to run `install.packages("dplyr")` and then load it with `library(dplyr)`.


```{r}
library(dplyr)

filter(gapminder, year==2004, country=="Mexico")
filter(gapminder, year==1966, country=="Mexico")

gapminder$year
```



> Q. Make a histogram of lifeExp fill color by continent

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) + 
  geom_histogram()

```



```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) + 
  geom_boxplot()
```
